paper_metadata.title: An efficient quantum algorithm for independent component analysis

experiments.description: Classical simulation of the proposed quantum ICA/KICA contrast-function estimation on synthetic mixtures sampled from specified probability density functions, used to study contrast landscape, measurement error sensitivity, sample-size scaling, and Amari error.

algorithm.variant: Quantum algorithm for adapted Kernel ICA contrast-function estimation
algorithm.optimizer: classical optimization on the Stiefel manifold via Cayley transform

hyperparameters.kappa: positive constant κ used in Rκ

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Samples x_ij are accessed through oracle O_xi|j⟩|0⟩ = |j⟩|x_ij⟩; Gram matrices are block-encoded and eigenvalues/eigenvectors estimated via phase estimation and amplitude estimation.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate det(R_κ(WPY)) where J(X) = -ln(det(R_κ(X))) and R_κ is built from low-rank Gram-matrix eigendecompositions.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Orthogonality enforced by whitening and optimization on the Stiefel manifold; no QUBO-style constraints.

problem_instance.description: Synthetic independent components drawn from given PDFs, linearly mixed by parameterized mixing matrices and then processed by the adapted KICA contrast function.

dataset_specification.description: Raw ICs sampled from given probability density functions (figure 6); mixtures generated by exp{iδP} and exp{i(δ1P1 + δ2P2)}; used to evaluate contrast values, norms of quantum states, query complexity, minimum eigenvalues, and Amari error.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Centering and whitening; covariance matrix estimation; construction of transformed samples y' = W M^{-1/2}(x - E[x]); Gaussian kernel Gram matrices; low-rank truncation to Mi = O(log N).
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Numerical simulation over varying N and mixing coefficients; measurement-error sweeps; Amari error computed versus known mixing matrix; repeated random mixtures for minimum-eigenvalue studies.

noise_model.noise_description: measurement error introduced in numerical experiments; no explicit physical noise model

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Centering, whitening, covariance estimation, classical computation of W M^{-1/2}, and generation of synthetic mixtures from PDFs.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classical reconstruction of R_κ and det(R_κ); Amari error computation; plotting of contrast landscapes and scaling curves.

speedup_claims.factor: exponential reduction in dependence on data scale; polylog(N) dependence in the optimization framework
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical ICA / KICA algorithms with at least Omega(N) scaling
speedup_claims.conditions: given qRAM access to samples and quantum preprocessing / matrix operations
speedup_claims.caveats: Speedup is for contrast-function estimation subroutine, not full end-to-end ICA; relies on quantum input model and low-rank Gram-matrix structure.

speedup_claims.conditions: for estimating det(R_kappa) with precision epsilon_1
speedup_claims.caveats: Formal theorem includes additional dependence on xi, epsilon_2, and mu_M.

scalability_data.metric_value: better than theoretical bound; fitted curve lgQ = 1.803 lg(1/eta) - 2.887(lg lg(1/eta))^2 + 8.291 lg lg(1/eta) - 0.530
increases linearly with quantum error epsilon_q and is unaffected by N

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: The paper claims contrast-function estimation complexity ˜O(ε_1^{-2} polylog(N/ε_1)) in the abstract; formal theorem gives ˜O(1/(ξ^2 ε_1^2) + μ_M/(ε_2 ||M||_2)) and near-independent case ˜O(1/(ε_1^2 ε_2) + μ_M/(ε_2 ||M||_2)).
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical ICA scaling is stated to be at least Ω(N); KICA involves Gram-matrix eigendecomposition and determinant computation.

experiments.description: Classical simulation of the proposed quantum ICA/KICA method on a transcriptomic lung-cancer dataset to separate latent independent components and compare them with stabilized-ICA (Icasso).

algorithm.variant: Quantum ICA / adapted KICA applied to transcriptomic source separation
algorithm.optimizer: classical optimization on the Stiefel manifold via Cayley transform

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Transcriptomic samples are treated as input vectors for the ICA preprocessing and Gram-matrix-based contrast evaluation.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize the adapted KICA contrast function J(X) = -ln(det(R_κ(X))) to recover independent components.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Whitening and orthogonal optimization on the Stiefel manifold.

problem_instance.description: Gene-expression data from patients with lung cancer; used to separate latent ICs and compare the resulting components with those from stabilized-ICA.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Transcriptomic dataset from Grossmann et al. 2017

dataset_specification.description: Gene-expression data for lung-cancer patients; compared against stabilized-ICA (Icasso) outputs; exact sample count and feature count not reported in the paper text provided.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Simplified optimization process; ICA preprocessing implied (centering/whitening) before contrast-function evaluation.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Correlation matrix between ICs separated by the proposed method and by stabilized-ICA; qualitative comparison of separated components.

implementation_details.classical_solver: stabilized-ICA (Icasso) package used as comparison baseline
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: ICA preprocessing implied; comparison baseline from stabilized-ICA.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Correlation matrix between separated ICs used for comparison.

speedup_claims.factor: exponential reduction in dependence on data scale; polylog(N) dependence in the optimization framework
speedup_claims.conditions: same quantum contrast-function estimation subroutine as main algorithm
speedup_claims.caveats: The transcriptomic experiment is a qualitative application; no runtime or qubit counts reported.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Same claimed contrast-function estimation scaling as the main algorithm: ˜O(ε_1^{-2} polylog(N/ε_1)) in the abstract; formal theorem bounds as above.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Not explicitly given for this experiment; stabilized-ICA is a classical baseline.

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical forecasting pipeline for the Nikkei 225 opening index using ICA-based noise reduction followed by support vector regression (QICA-SVR), compared against ICA-SVR and SVR baselines.

algorithm.optimizer: SVR training; ICA preprocessing optimized by classical Stiefel-manifold methods

problem_formulation.encoding_details: ICA preprocessing uses sample oracles and Gram-matrix estimation; SVR operates on the ICA-transformed classical features.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Predict the Nikkei 225 opening cash index from four forecasting variables after ICA-based denoising; ICA objective is to minimize J(X) = -ln(det(R_κ(X))).
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: ICA orthogonality via whitening and Stiefel-manifold optimization; SVR constraints handled by standard ε-insensitive regression.

problem_instance.description: Financial time-series forecasting of the Nikkei 225 opening cash index.

dataset_specification.description: Daily data from 5 June 2015 to 9 September 2016; four forecasting variables: previous day’s cash market closing index and three Nikkei 225 futures contracts traded on Singapore Exchange-Derivative Trading Limited, Osaka Securities Exchange, and Chicago Mercantile Exchange; first 300 points used for preprocessing, last 100 for testing, with training on samples 100 through 301 as stated in the paper.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Centering, normalization, and noise reduction by ICA; least important IC discarded from forecasting variables.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Reported normalized mean squared error (NMSE) and consistency (Cons) for multiple C and ε settings; comparison against ICA-SVR and SVR baselines.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Support Vector Regression (SVR); ICA-SVR and SVR baselines
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Centering, normalization, ICA-based noise reduction, and discarding the least important IC.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: SVR prediction of the opening index; evaluation by NMSE and consistency.

speedup_claims.conditions: forecasting task on Nikkei 225 opening index
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports improved predictive performance, not computational speedup, for the hybrid pipeline.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: The ICA preprocessing/contrast estimation is claimed to scale as ˜O(ε_1^{-2} polylog(N/ε_1)); the overall hybrid pipeline is not given a full end-to-end complexity.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Not explicitly given for the SVR pipeline.
